summary: Presigned range GETs modified by TCP segmentation offload / WAN optimizer leading to TLS boundary re-splitting and presigned signature validation failures on Private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403/Integrity errors when the serving nodes fetch large model shard ranges via presigned range GETs through their corporate WAN optimizer / TCP offload appliance. Failures correlate with large-range requests (>8MB) and only happen from the customer's VPC endpoint to S3-like storage.

Impact:
- Model pulls fail intermittently during startup, causing node rollout delays and degraded capacity.
- Partial shard reads cause checksum/integrity verification failures, triggering retries and slower cold-start times.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC endpoint + on-prem WAN optimizer in path)
- Customer-managed egress appliance with TCP segmentation offload (TSO) and MSS clamping enabled
- Observed from serving nodes in us-east-1 retrieving model shards from artifact storage using presigned range URLs

Observed behaviour:
- S3 GETs with Range: bytes=... return 403 or incomplete content on validation, or the object is fetched but fails checksum validation on the serving node.
- When requests are retried from a different IP/path, they sometimes succeed.

Expected behaviour:
- Presigned range requests should be fetched intact; serving nodes should validate checksums and proceed to load model shard without content mismatch or 403s.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a private cluster connected via customer-managed egress appliance with TSO enabled.
2) Trigger a cold start that causes serving nodes to download a large shard (>8MB) via a presigned range GET through the customer's VPCE.
3) Observe the artifact download logs and checksum validation on the serving node.
4) Repeat with TSO and MSS clamping disabled on the appliance (if possible) for control test.
logs:
- Serving node logs: checksum mismatch for shard model-2026-03-09-8mb.part at byte range 0-8388607; computed sha256 != manifest.
- HTTP trace: 200 OK but Content-Length mismatch reported by the node, subsequent validation fails.
- Packet capture summary (customer-provided): TLS records split such that application-level range boundaries do not align with expected chunking; occasional retransmit and sequence reassembly differences.
- VPCE access logs: successful GETs with status 200, followed by application-level checksum failure on node side.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage - customer reports ~15% failure rate for large range downloads, intermittent and correlated with peak WAN optimizer activity.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (FinWave): We confirmed disabling the WAN optimizer TSO feature reduced failures in a short test window (not fully validated across fleet). Attached pcap and node logs.

2026-03-11 08:40 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Collected server-side trace and compared with customer pcap. Observed TLS record re-segmentation and differences in TCP payload alignment for range boundaries. Hypothesis: TSO/MSS clamping in middlebox modifies segmentation and leads to signature validation edge cases for presigned range processing.

2026-03-11 13:18 - Eng (Storage): Note - presigned signatures are computed over the canonical request; the backend does not sign per-TLS-record boundaries, but if proxies mutate headers or reassemble range chunks incorrectly then the request can hit signature checks or range reassembly bugs downstream. Looking into how intermediate segmentation could cause partial-range retransmit anomalies.

2026-03-12 10:04 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Requested packet captures that include TLS record sizes and observed MSS clamp to 1200 bytes in several flows. Customer schedule for controlled test tomorrow to toggle TSO/MSS clamp.
2026-03-12 14:30 - Customer (FinWave): Confirmed controlled test: disabling TSO reduced failed fetches from 15% to <1% over 2 hours. Re-enabling with MSS set to default reproduced failures.
investigation_notes:
- Reproducible correlation between TCP segmentation offload / MSS clamp and failure rate.
- Packet captures show TLS records being split across different TCP segments that do not preserve the original HTTP range request framing after middlebox reassembly.
- Hypothesis: Customer WAN optimizer performs packet coalescing/segmentation modifications that can cause the VPCE/S3 presigned validation or downstream caching proxies to mis-evaluate the range request or to serve partial content from cache leading to checksum mismatch.
- Storage team reviewed S3-like gateway logs; gateway returns 200 for range requests but sometimes serves cached partial response when malformed Range header or connection reordering occurs.
- No evidence of credential/key compromise; failures appear to be due to in-flight request transformation.
- Control experiments by toggling TSO on the appliance strongly reduce failures, indicating middlebox behavior as root contributor.
resolution:
Workaround documented: advise customer to disable TSO/GSO on WAN optimizer or set MSS/clamp to avoid small MSS values (recommend MSS >= 1460) for flows to VPCE and artifact storage.
Permanent follow-ups: 1) Storage team to harden range handling to better tolerate re-segmentation anomalies and avoid serving partial cached ranges when Range header appears malformed. 2) Update private-deploy runbook with guidance for middleboxes (TSO/GSO/MSS) and presigned URL validation edge cases. 3) Create engineering ticket to add validation telemetry in serving nodes to differentiate between transport-level truncation vs object corruption.
Status: customer accepted workaround and will schedule WAN appliance config change; engineering backlog items created referenced in linked_issues and related_github_prs.
